absent: Layout and synchronization of global audit-signal pid, uid and label storage.
Recognition criteria for the audit daemon task and login, session and security attribute retrieval.
Capacity value and overflow policy details for auxiliary pid blocks beyond allocation failure signals.
Filter rule structure, hash placement, duplication, deletion and RCU reclamation contracts.
Audit log buffer lifecycle, formatting, key handling and configuration-change record schema.
Filesystem notification group, mark reference counting and event delivery guarantees.
Control lock and filter mutex ownership, nesting with other locks and interrupt context rules.
Prune worker creation, wakeup signaling, shutdown and scheduling interactions.
Audit context allocation, dummy detection, current context retrieval and tree reference handling.
Network namespace handling and netlink queueing for audit message distribution.

findings.text: Exposes signal auditing hook for delivered signals. When the destination is the audit daemon and the number belongs to the termination or user-defined set, it snapshots sender thread-group identity, login or fallback user identity, and caller security label into global audit-signal state, then forwards to the per-operation recorder and propagates that result.

Provides per-operation recording of signal recipients for audit trail correlation. The initial recipient is retained directly in the current operation context while additional recipients accumulate in chained bounded auxiliary blocks, each entry capturing thread-group identity, login and user identities, session, command name and object security label.

Signal recipient recording is skipped without error when global signal auditing is off, when no usable operation context exists, or in the header fallback that always reports success. Overflow handling reports allocation failure when a new auxiliary block cannot be obtained and invalid input when a block is already at capacity.

Defines three progressive per-task audit modes: disabled with no per-task context or syscall records, build with context creation and entry-time fill available on demand, and record with context creation plus mandatory entry fill and exit emission.

Rule list node pairs linkage and deferred reclamation with an embedded filter rule. Capability snapshot holds permitted, inheritable, ambient and root identity plus either file effective bit or process effective set through a shared slot.

Path component record carries name reference and log length, visibility and lifetime flags, filesystem identity and ownership attributes, object security label, file capability snapshot with version, and record type. Process title record carries command-line length and value pointer.
Event identifier pairs syscall entry wall time with a serial number.

Core operation context anchors per-syscall and io-uring auditing with lifecycle state, event identity, invoked operation identity and arguments, outcome and priority, inline plus overflow name collection, rule key, filesystem and network context, saved credential snapshot, and tree-watch bookkeeping, with a leading dummy marker and usage discriminator.

Extended operation context retains primary signal-target identity with command name and security reference, file descriptor pair and process title, a type tag, and a variant payload covering socketcall, interprocess, message queue control and transfer, queue creation, capability update, mapping, open, execution, module, and time disciplines.
Count of preallocated name slots inside each operation context is five.
Count of inode hash buckets used for watch and rule lookup is thirty two.
Sentinel requesting full-path parent derivation during name comparison is negative one.
Filesystem event sets for mark and watch handling cover move, create, delete and self-move or self-delete, with unmount additionally covered for watches and group duplication enabled for marks.
Netlink peer record binds a port identifier and network namespace to an outbound queue. Watch comparison context carries directory and child inode references.
Filesystem mark wrapper binds device and inode identity plus insertion path to an underlying filesystem notification mark and owning filter rule.

Directory-tree watch family links reference-counted trees with gone flag, root chunk pointer, chunk and rule lists and pathname suffix; chunks carry hash linkage, key, notification mark, resident tree list, owner count with counted owner array and reference counters; tree marks bind notification mark to chunk.

Path-watch family links reference-counted watches with device, path, inode number, parent pointer, parent-membership linkage and rule anchor; parents anchor member watches and carry a notification mark.
Parent-length helper reports the byte length of the directory prefix including its separator, ignoring empty input and redundant trailing separators and stopping at the last remaining separator.

Name comparison reports mismatch when the candidate path is shorter than the entry, otherwise compares only the final component after stripping trailing separators, deriving the parent offset from the path itself when full-path mode is requested.

Mark event handling verifies group ownership, then on create or move or delete it refreshes the watched inode when the affected name matches the stored path, while on self-delete, unmount or self-move it logs automatic removal and deletes the owning rule.

Tree lifecycle moves doomed trees either to a global prune queue serviced by a sleeping background worker or to the current operation postponed list, with eviction detaching all trees rooted at a chunk and kill processing draining the postponed list, each victim removed from its queue before pruning.

Initialization entry points allocate filesystem notification groups with dedicated operation tables, prepare caches and hash anchors, and report allocation failures through audit panic paths while leaving null group state for marks.

Background prune and synchronous kill paths serialize with the control lock outermost and the filter mutex inside, temporarily releasing the filter mutex around per-victim pruning while retaining control serialization across the drain.

Eviction serializes tree detachment with filter mutex outermost and hash spin protection inside, dropping hash protection around per-owner relocation. Mark freeing serializes with group lock outermost and hash protection inside while detaching the chunk reference.

Watch refresh holds the filter mutex across matching, duplication and rule rehashing, releasing only on early miss or after installing the replacement watch, and panics without install when duplication fails.

Unexpected states are contained by one-time warnings for group mismatch or auxiliary overflow, a fatal guard for under-referenced marks during freeing, and a build-time fatal placeholder for tree killing when tree support is compiled out.

Tree lookup by inode key walks the corresponding hash chain under read-side protection and only on key equality acquires a reference and returns the chunk, otherwise reports absence. Membership test scans owner slots for exact tree pointer equality.

Chunk reclamation drops owner tree references and frees storage only after the last long-lived reference is released, with a read-cycle callback bridging to the counted release and a cache destructor for tree marks.

Watch helpers compare device and inode identity unless unset, duplicate path and identity with shared parent reference, and refresh bindings for the single watch whose stored path matches the triggering name by rebuilding its rules onto a new hash placement.

Rule-change logging emits configuration-change records with session context, operation label, untrusted path, rule key, list number and success result when auditing is enabled, and automatic removal couples that logging with rule deletion.
Postponed-tree accessor yields no list when no operation context exists or the context is unused, otherwise yields the context-owned killed-trees queue.

Disabled-configuration header provides inclusion guard and inert fallbacks: watch acquisition and inode filtering expand to no-ops, watch comparison always reports mismatch, executable duplication always reports invalid argument, and tree termination always faults.

Global notification state holds distinct filesystem groups for path marks, directory trees and inode watches, a dedicated prune worker handle, a tree-mark cache, and a fixed hash table with cache-aligned spin protection for chunk lookup.
Chunk hash table size is one hundred twenty eight.

Mark destruction releases wrapper resources: path-mark teardown frees stored path and wrapper via container retrieval, watch teardown frees parent holder, and tree teardown returns the mark to its dedicated cache, with tree freeing additionally detaching and evicting the bound chunk.
Tree inode event handler is inert and always reports success, with all lifecycle effects deferred to mark freeing and eviction.
